key_insight: Sampling Feynman paths from both circuit endpoints improves classical Monte Carlo estimation of quantum transition amplitudes over forward-only sampling.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers memory-efficient circuit amplitude estimation, with computational cost governed by estimator variance rather than exhaustive path enumeration.
method: Launch random walks from the input and output computational basis states.
Combine forward and backward walks into bidirectionally sampled Feynman paths.
Use Multiple Importance Sampling to reduce variance from low-probability paths.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports faster empirical convergence than forward-only sampling and demonstrations on circuits with up to 4096 qubits.
watch_item: Practical runtime remains variance-dependent; the reported qubit count alone does not establish efficiency for arbitrary circuits.
paper_title: Bidirectional Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation of Quantum Circuits
